environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; scripted peer emitting exact response bytes, hexdump of client output

findings.description: The build keeps the first head and resizes the buffered output to the interim Content-Length, so the real 200 that follows is cut to that many bytes and arrives as body text: an interim Content-Length of 20 yields the tail HTTP/1.1 200 OK CRLF Con and nothing more. The client has a body that is a fragment of a head. Precondition: an attacker-influenced upstream.
findings.title: A 1xx is treated as terminal and its Content-Length truncates the following real head mid-line

limitations: All RCE is on the upstream host
methods: Read the release source from the tag
Diffed the release source against the staged copy (identical)
Control response first on the same config
Scripted peer emitted one interim shape per path
Captured client bytes as hex and diffed against the control
Sent a follow-up request on the same connection
